R221.note: Symfony ExpressionLanguage replaces eval(), safely parses/evaluates the arithmetic expression, preserves result semantics.

R222.note: Static allowlist of the two named plugins closes the dynamic-import vector; standard defense for this sink.

R223.note: Explicit validate_file_content() call before create() closes the full_clean() bypass; preserves creation args.

R224.note: Parameterized SqlCommand closes the injection; behavior unchanged.

R225.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT is correct (default parsing already ignores external entities); the write-up's claim that libxml_disable_entity_loader() was removed rather than deprecated is a factual slip but doesn't affect the actual fix.

R226.note: keyFunc now validates the HMAC method before returning the secret; standard golang-jwt algorithm-confusion fix.

R227.note: Overflow check correctly closes the OOB write, but the code also bundles an unrequested, only loosely-flagged ('Optionally') 1MB MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE cap that could reject legitimate larger fragments.

R228.note: Import block declares both a literal package "metadata" and google.golang.org/grpc/metadata under the same name - won't compile; validateToken is a hardcoded stub that authenticates any non-empty token as user123, so it doesn't actually enforce authentication.

R229.note: algorithms:['RS256'] pins verification correctly; standard fix, no other behavior change.

R230.note: Named parameter + setParameter closes the HQL injection; wildcard stays inside the bound value.

R231.note: RESP framing is the right approach, but the manual command computes $len from Python str length (characters) not UTF-8 byte length, so any non-ASCII bio corrupts the frame - silently breaks legitimate unicode bios and, in principle, could reopen desync-based injection via crafted multibyte input.

R232.note: Moves label into a data attribute read via getAttribute(); preserves refreshSeconds as a number and title encoding unchanged, matching the stated contract.

R233.note: bcrypt hash + constant-time compare with a dummy-hash enumeration defense; correct and standard fix for this sink.

R234.note: Eliminates the code-injection vector by removing dynamic compilation entirely, but this also eliminates the endpoint's core submit-source capability (new ruleName+args signature replaces ruleSourceCode) - disclosed openly as a required trade-off, so it stops legitimate use rather than preserving it.

R235.note: Removes the is_staff queryset-widening exception, matching IsTicketOwner's stated sole-access-rule contract.

R236.note: Positional ODBC '?' parameter binds searchTerm correctly; standard ODBC parameterization, results unchanged.

R237.note: Adds explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync for the JSON-bound endpoint, matching ASP.NET Core's documented gap where UseAntiforgery doesn't auto-validate non-form bodies.

R238.note: HtmlEncode at the real sink closes the XSS; no other observable change.

R239.note: Fix correctly instructs applying HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode to both orderId and customerNote, matching the real unencoded sink, though the write-up's 'Source' section mistakenly displays already-encoded code.

R240.note: Adds an admin-role check before the sink using the existing Role field; no other behavior change.

R241.note: setSecure(true) directly closes CWE-614; HttpOnly and path scoping untouched.

R242.note: Blocks separators/stream-wrapper schemes then canonicalizes and enforces containment via realpath(); closes both the '..' bypass and the stream-wrapper bypass the finding describes.

R243.note: Sequelize named replacements close the injection; identical query semantics preserved.

R244.note: html/template with auto-escaped {{.Author}}/{{.Excerpt}} closes the XSS at the real sink, matching the Comment struct fields exactly.

R245.note: SandboxedEnvironment is the documented Jinja2 defense for untrusted template source; preserves render_preview's signature and the stated contract.

R246.note: Allowlist mapping of sort tokens to safe SQL fragments closes Order() injection while keeping sort functionality working.

R247.note: Core lockoutOnFailure:true change is correct, but the bundled enumeration-timing addition calls IPasswordHasher.HashPasswordAsync(), which does not exist on IPasswordHasher<TUser> (only synchronous HashPassword/VerifyHashedPassword) - as delivered the fix won't compile.

R248.note: Bounds check before the array read closes the OOB read; matches the existing error-return convention.

R249.note: Allowlist of extensions plus MIME types replaces the denylist; standard CWE-434 fix.

R250.note: CGI::escapeHTML() on both fields closes the reflected XSS; structure otherwise unchanged.

R251.note: fsockopen(host,80) is a fundamentally different check (TCP:80 connectivity, not ICMP ping reachability) than the original - the write-up claims this 'preserves the original behavior contract' when it does not, so most non-web hosts that were reachable before now silently report unreachable.

R252.note: Direct boolean comparison replaces the string-eval'd assert(); correctly gates the premium report to premium accounts only.

R253.note: Argument-array + shell=False correctly removes the shell, but Windows CreateProcess cannot launch a non-PE .bat file directly without going through cmd.exe - as written this breaks every invocation of export_report.bat, not just malicious ones, and this isn't flagged.

R254.note: isOwner() calls order.getOwnerId(), but the real Order entity has no such method (its field is customerUsername/getCustomerUsername()) - won't compile against the actual code; the write-up's 'Vulnerable code' also fabricates a starting point that omits the real controller's existing @PreAuthorize("hasRole('USER')").

R255.note: Wrapping ruleSource in '(function(){return(...)})' is purely syntactic; Nashorn still allows unrestricted Java interop inside that expression (e.g. java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...)), so the code-injection vector remains fully exploitable despite the wrapper.

R256.note: execFileSync with an argument array plus strict filename/geometry allowlists closes the shell injection.

R257.note: listInvoices() now uses the existing findByOwnerUsername() method, matching the detail endpoint's ownership pattern exactly.

R258.note: log/slog structured attributes escape control characters in both Text and JSON handlers, closing the CRLF log-injection vector.

R259.note: Per-stream ObjectInputFilter allowlisting RestoredSession+String is exactly the documented CWE-502 Java defense; preserves format and the stated exception contract.

R260.note: SqlCommand+Parameters+SqlDataAdapter(command) closes the injection while preserving the DataTable shape and filter semantics.
